text: A new `sqllens verify-memory PATH [--format json|csv] [--fail-under PCT] [-c CONFIG]` CLI command exists, matching the existing command conventions in `cli.py`.
The golden file is parsed with the existing memory-bundle parser (`question,sql` JSON/CSV via `parse_json` / `parse_csv`); no new file format is introduced.
Each case is classified PASS / CHANGED / ERROR using `sqlglot`-normalized SQL comparison against the configured database dialect.
The runner forces `show_details` on so `query_info["sql"]` is populated for each case, and extracts the agent's generated SQL from it.
Output is a per-case table plus a summary line; every non-PASS case shows the expected-vs-actual SQL.
Exit code is non-zero when any case is not PASS (or, when `--fail-under` is given, when the PASS rate is below the threshold).

Per CLAUDE.md, an **empty golden set**, an **all-ERROR run**, or a **partial failure** surfaces as a loud non-success — never a green/empty success. (An empty golden file is itself an error: there is nothing to verify, so the command must not exit 0.)
The SQL-normalization comparator is isolated (`compare.py`) so a future "execute and compare rows" comparator can be added without rewriting the runner.
New `.py` files under `src/sqllens/eval/` carry the SPDX header and pass `ruff check .` (this package is **not** in the vendored-exclusion set) and have type hints on every public signature.
